Why self-supervision?
Supervised learning needs many pairs (x, y). Labels are often expensive, slow, or noisy, while
unlabeled x is cheap and abundant.

Goal.
Learn an encoder fθ that maps x 7→h useful for many downstream tasks, then attach a
small head with few labels. If a method adds a projector, h →g →z and the loss uses z; keep h
for downstream.
Transfer mindset.
1. Pretrain on unlabeled data with a pretext objective.
2. Adapt to the real task (linear probe or fine-tune).
Self-supervised learning is not “no supervision”: it is supervision invented from the data.

Self-supervised pretraining
Figure 3: Self-supervised pretraining pipeline. Gray = data; orange = compute. The pretext
head is often discarded after pretraining.
Pretext task.
A problem we design so that solving it forces the encoder to capture useful
structure. The target is computed automatically from x (rotation angle, reconstruction of x,
agreement of two views, next token, masked content, . . . ).
Encoder fθ.
Backbone (CNN, MLP, . . . ). Output: representation h of fixed width. This is the
asset we keep. (Transformer backbones appear in later chapters.)
Representation h.
Encoder output h is the reusable feature. A good h preserves semantics
and discards nuisance noise. Judge quality by downstream metrics, not pretext accuracy alone.
Projection z = g(h) (if any) is only for the pretraining loss and is typically discarded.
Pretext head.
Small network on top of h (classifier, decoder, projector, . . . ) that defines the
pretraining loss. Usually thrown away before the real task.

Contrastive learning (SimCLR)
Core idea.
Two augmented views of the same image should match; views of different images
should not.
Roles.
Encoder f: representation h kept for downstream. Projector g: map h →z used only
for the contrastive loss; discard g after pretraining. Both f and g are weight-shared across views.

Batch similarity (idea)
+ = positive (two views of same sample)
−= negative (other samples)
empty diagonal = ignored (not a negative)
Figure 13: Positives (+), negatives (−), empty diagonal = ignored.
EMA teacher.
θteacher ←m θteacher + (1 −m) θstudent,
m ∈(0, 1) (often ≈0.996).
Teacher updates slowly; no backprop through teacher — stable soft targets.
Key ingredients.
• Multi-crop views (global + local) of the same image.
• Student matches teacher softmax (CE / KL-style).
• Centering / sharpening on teacher outputs to avoid collapse.
• Keep the student encoder for downstream.
Centering (concrete).
Let teacher logits be ℓt ∈RK. Maintain a running center c:
c ←mc c + (1 −mc) Ebatch[ℓt],
ℓt ←ℓt −c,
pt = softmax(ℓt/τt).
Without centering, one slot can dominate for every image (trivial constant prediction). Centering
removes a global bias so slots compete fairly. Sharpening uses a smaller teacher temperature τt
so pt is peakier (harder to match with a collapsed uniform).

title: Fine-tune.
text:
Fine-tune.
Update f (often smaller LR) + task head. Stronger when some labels exist; risk of
overwriting pretrained features if too aggressive.
Pitfalls.
Evaluating only pretext accuracy; domain shift; train/test leakage; augmentations /
masks that leak the answer.
When SSL helps.
Labels scarce; related unlabeled data plentiful; transfer across tasks in the
same modality. May not help if data are tiny and domains mismatch, or if labels are already
abundant.
10
Code view
for x in unlabeled_loader :
x1 , x2 = augment(x), augment(x)
# two views
h1 , h2 = encoder(x1), encoder(x2)
# shared f
z1 , z2 = projector(h1), projector(h2) # shared g
loss = nt_xent(z1 , z2 , tau)
loss.backward (); opt.step ()
# later: discard
projector; train
task head on encoder(h)
Useful docs: torchvision.transforms, torchvision.models, TF data augmentation, keras.application
Minimal project checklist.
Pick a family; fix encoder dim; log pretext loss; evaluate with a
linear probe early; only then fine-tune.
11
Exercises
1. Draw the SSL pipeline and mark which blocks are discarded after pretrain.
2. Contrast AE vs SimCLR: what is the pretext target in each case?
3. For a batch of N=2 images (4 views), mark + / −/ ignored cells as in Figure 13.
4. Write the EMA update for a DINO teacher; explain why m ≈1.
5. Explain centering: what goes wrong if one teacher logit dimension always dominates?
6. Next-token vs masked: who can see the future? What is the label?
References
• T. Chen et al., SimCLR, 2020.
• K. He et al., MoCo, 2020; J.-B. Grill et al., BYOL, 2020.
• M. Caron et al., DINO, 2021; M. Oquab et al., DINOv2, 2023.
• K. He et al., MAE, 2021; A. Radford et al., CLIP, 2021; M. Assran et al., I-JEPA, 2023.
• J. Devlin et al., BERT (MLM); A. Radford et al., GPT / next-token LM (Transformers
chapter).
• S. Gidaris et al., Rotation prediction, 2018.
